This alone suffices to describe the Qur'an and indicates its rank.

{2} But along with this, He increased its clarification of its perfection by the One upon whom it was sent down, Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the noblest of creation. Whatever it indicates is the greatest type of truth among all knowledge-based matters, and beyond the truth there is only error.

{3} {Unquestionably, to Allah belongs the pure religion}: This is an affirmation of the command to sincerity, and an explanation that just as perfection belongs entirely to Him, and He is bounteous to His servants in every respect, so too the pure religion, free of all impurities, belongs to Him. It is the religion He has approved for Himself, and approved for the elite of His creation, and commanded them with, because it includes devotion to Allah in His love, fear, and hope, and turning to Him in worship, and turning to Him in obtaining the needs of His servants. This is what reforms hearts, purifies them and cleanses them, unlike associating partners with Him in any act of worship. Indeed Allah is free of it, and there is no share for Allah in it. He is the most independent of partners from partnership, and it corrupts hearts, souls, this world and the Hereafter, and wearies souls to the utmost wretchedness.
Therefore, when He commanded monotheism and sincerity, He forbade associating partners with Him, and informed of the blame for those who associate partners with Him, saying: {And those who take protectors besides Him}; that is, they take them as allies through worshipping and calling upon them, making excuses for themselves and saying: {We only worship them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position}; that is, so that they may raise our needs to Allah and intercede for us with Him. Otherwise, we know that they do not create, nor provide, nor possess anything of the command. These people have abandoned what Allah commanded of sincerity, and have dared to commit the greatest of the prohibited acts, which is shirk. They have compared the One to whom nothing is similar, the Great King, with kings, and they claimed by their corrupt minds and their sickly opinion that just as kings cannot be reached except through dignitaries, intercessors and ministers who raise the needs of their subjects to them, and who win their compassion for them and pave the way for them in that matter, so too is Allah, exalted is He!
This analogy is among the most corrupt of analogies, for it entails equating the Creator with the created, despite the clear difference established by reason, transmitted text and innate nature. Kings only needed intermediaries between themselves and their subjects because they do not know their conditions, so someone is needed to inform them of their conditions. Perhaps there is no mercy in their hearts toward the one in need, so someone is needed to incline them toward him and ask them for mercy for him. They need intercessors and ministers, and they fear them, so they grant the needs of those who have interceded for them, out of consideration for them and to placate their feelings. They are also poor, and may withhold out of fear of poverty. As for the Lord, exalted is He, His knowledge encompasses outward and inward matters, He needs no one to inform Him of the conditions of His subjects and servants, He is the Most Merciful of the merciful and the Most Generous of the generous, and He has no need for any of His creatures to make him merciful to His servants. Rather, He is more merciful to them than they are to themselves and than their parents are. He urges them and calls them to the means by which they attain His mercy, He desires for them what is better for them than what they desire for themselves, and He is the Self-Sufficient, to whom belongs complete and absolute self-sufficiency. Were all creation, from first to last, gathered in one plain and asked of Him, and He gave each of them what he asked for and wished, it would not diminish His self-sufficiency in the least, and they would not diminish what He has, except as a needle diminishes the sea when dipped into it. All intercessors fear Him, so none of them intercedes except with His permission, and to Him belongs all intercession. By these distinctions, the ignorance of the polytheists regarding Him, their great foolishness, and the severity of their audacity against Him are known. It is also known the wisdom in the fact that Allah does not forgive shirk, because it includes disparagement of Allah, exalted is He. For this reason, He said, judging between the sincere believers and the polytheists, and implicitly threatening the polytheists: {Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ}. It is known that His judgment is that the sincere believers are in gardens of bliss, and that whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden Paradise to him, and his abode is the Fire. {Indeed, Allah does not guide}; that is, does not grant success in guidance to the straight path {one who is a liar and a disbeliever}; that is, one who is characterized by lying or disbelief, such that admonitions and signs come to him and what he is characterized by does not depart from him, and Allah shows him the signs and he denies them, disbelieves in them and lies. How can such a one attain guidance, when he has closed the door upon himself? He is punished by having Allah seal his heart, so he does not believe.

**(6)** And from His might is that ﴿He created you from one soul﴾, despite your multitude and your dispersal throughout the regions of the earth. ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾, so that he might find tranquility in her and she in him, and thereby His blessing is completed. ﴿And He sent down for you from the grazing livestock﴾, meaning He created them by a decree that descends from Him as a mercy to you, ﴿eight mates﴾, which are those He mentioned in Surah al-An'am: ﴿eight mates: two of the sheep, two of the goats, two of the camels, and two of the cattle﴾. Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 39, verse 8:

{8} He, exalted is He, informs of His generosity toward His servant, His kindness, His beneficence, and the scant thankfulness of His servant. When harm touches him, whether illness, poverty, or falling into the distress of a sea-voyage or other calamity, he knows that none can rescue him in that state except Allah. So he calls upon Him, humbly and turning in repentance, and seeks His aid in removing what has befallen him, and persists in this. ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself﴾: that is, by removing from him the harm and distress, ﴿he forgets what he was calling upon Him for before﴾; that is, he forgets that harm for which he called upon Allah, and passes on as though no harm had ever touched him, and he persists in his polytheism, ﴿and sets up rivals to Allah in order to lead [others] astray from His way﴾; that is, so that he himself goes astray and leads others astray, because leading astray is a branch of being astray, so the verse mentions the cause (the consequence) to indicate the effect (what follows from it). ﴿Say﴾ to this rebellious one who has exchanged Allah's favor for disbelief: ﴿Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; you are indeed among the companions of the Fire﴾: so what you enjoy will not benefit you if the final destination is the Fire. ﴿Have you considered: if We grant them enjoyment for years, then there comes to them what they were promised? Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 39, verse 9:

{9} This is a comparison between the one who acts in obedience to God and the one who does not, and between the knowledgeable and the ignorant. This is among the matters whose difference is established in the intellects and whose disparity is known with certain knowledge. The one who turns away from obedience to his Lord and follows his desires is not like the one who is ﴿qanit﴾ (devoutly obedient); that is, one who obeys God with the best of acts of worship, which is the prayer (salah), and the best of times, which are the hours of the night. So He described him with abundance of action and its excellence. Then He described him with fear and hope, and mentioned that the object of fear is the punishment of the Hereafter for the sins that have preceded, and that the object of hope is the mercy of God. Thus He described him with outward and inward action.

{Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?} Those who know their Lord and know His legislated religion (dinuhu al-shar'i) and His religion of recompense (dinuhu al-jaza'i), and the secrets and wisdoms in that, {and those who do not know} anything of that. Those two are not equal, just as the night and the day, the shade and the heat, and the water and the fire are not equal.

{It is only those of understanding who are reminded} when they are admonished, {those of understanding (ulu al-albab)}; that is, people of pure and sharp intellects. They are the ones who prefer the higher over the lower, so they prefer knowledge over ignorance and obedience to God over opposing Him, because they have intellects that guide them to consider the consequences, unlike the one who has no understanding (lubb) and no intellect, for he takes his desire as his god.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 39, verse 10:

{10} That is: say, calling out to the noblest of creation, who are the believers, commanding them with the best of commands, which is taqwa (God-consciousness), mentioning to them the cause that necessitates taqwa, which is God's lordship over them and His bounty upon them, which requires of them that they fear Him. Among this is what God has bestowed upon them of faith, for it necessitates taqwa, just as you say: "O generous one, give charity!" and "O brave one, fight!" He also mentioned to them the reward that encourages them in this world, saying: {For those who do good in this world}, by worshipping their Lord, {is a good}: abundant provision, a tranquil soul, and an expanded heart, as He, the Exalted, said: {Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life}. {And the earth of Allah is spacious}: if you are prevented from worshipping Him in one land, then emigrate to another, where you may worship your Lord and be able to establish your religion.

When He said {For those who do good in this world is a good}, there was room in some souls for this objection: the text is general, that whoever does good has a good in this world, so why is it that one who believes in a land where he is persecuted and humiliated does not obtain that? He dispelled this assumption with His words {And the earth of Allah is spacious}. Here is a good tiding which the Prophet (ﷺ) stated explicitly when he said: "A group of my nation will continue to be upon the truth, prevailing; those who forsake them or oppose them will not harm them, until the command of Allah comes while they are still upon that." This verse points to it and aims at it from close by, namely that He, the Exalted, informed that His earth is spacious; so whenever you are prevented from worshipping Him in one place, emigrate to another. This is general across every time and place, so every emigrant must have a refuge among the Muslims to take shelter in, and a place where he is able to establish his religion.

{Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account}: this is general across all kinds of patience: patience upon God's painful decrees, so one does not rage against them; patience from His disobediences, so one does not commit them; and patience upon His obedience until one performs it. God promised the patient their reward without account; that is, without limit, without counting, and without measure. This is only due to the excellence of patience and its standing with God, and that it is a helper in all matters.

So whenever the one who reflects contemplates it, and the one who thinks deeply ponders it, he sees in its consistency, even in its obscure meanings, what dazzles the observers and convinces them that it could only have come from One who is All-Wise and All-Knowing. And if a meaning were repeated upon it only once throughout the whole Qur'an, it would not have an effect on it, and the result would not be achieved from it.

Rather, every place's explanation is complete in its meaning, without relying on what has passed of similar material. Although some places may be more extensive than others and more beneficial, this is how the reader of the Qur'an who reflects on its meanings should be: he should not neglect reflection on all places of it, for through that he obtains much good and abundant benefit. And since the Mighty Qur'an is of this majesty and greatness, it affects the hearts of the people of understanding who are guided. Therefore He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it, then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, because of what it contains of frightening and alarming warning, {then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah}; that is, at the mention of hope and encouragement. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 39, verses 32–35:

{32} Allah, exalted is He, says, warning and informing that there is no one more unjust, and none greater in injustice, than {the one who lies against Allah}: either by attributing to Him what is not befitting to His majesty, or by claiming prophethood, or by reporting that Allah said such-and-such, or related such-and-such, or ruled such-and-such while he is lying. This falls under His saying: {and that you say about Allah what you do not know} (2:169). If he is ignorant, [it is an offense]; otherwise it is even more heinous and more heinous. Or {denies the truth [of the Truth] when it has come to him}; that is: there is no one more unjust than the one to whom the truth, supported by clear proofs, has come, and he denies it. His denial is therefore a great injustice on his part, because he rejects the truth after it has become clear to him. If he combines lying against Allah with denying the truth, it is injustice upon injustice. {Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?} In it they are punished, and through it the rights of Allah are taken from every wrongdoer and disbeliever. {Indeed, association [of others with Allah] is a great wrong} (31:13).

{33} Having mentioned the liar who denies, his wrongdoing and his punishment, He mentioned the truthful one who confirms and his reward, saying: {And he who brings the truth}: in his statement and his deed. This includes the prophets and those who take their place among those who spoke truthfully concerning the news and rulings of Allah, and who practised the qualities of truthfulness. {And believes in it}; that is, in the truth. For a person may bring the truth, yet not believe in it, because of arrogance or contempt for the one who said it and brought it. Therefore praise requires both truthfulness and confirmation. His truthfulness indicates his knowledge and justice, and his confirmation indicates his humility and freedom from arrogance. {Those}; that is, those who were granted success in combining the two matters {are the righteous}: for all the qualities of piety return to speaking the truth and believing in it.

{34} {For them is whatever they wish with their Lord}: of reward that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to the heart of a human being. Whatever their wills and desires attach to, of kinds of pleasures and delights, is available to them, prepared and readied. {That is the reward of the good-doers}: those who worship Allah as though they see Him; for if they do not see Him, He sees them. They are the ones who do good to the servants of Allah.

{35} {That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do}: a person's deeds have three states: either worst, or best, or neither worst nor best. The last category is that of permissible acts, which carry neither reward nor punishment. The worst are all sins, and the best are all acts of obedience. By this detail the meaning of the verse becomes clear: His saying {that Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did} means their minor and major sins, because of their good-doing and piety. {And reward them their due for the best of what they used to do} means for all their good deeds. {Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward} (4:40).

{42} He, may He be exalted, informs that He alone has sole control over His servants, both in their wakefulness and their sleep, and in their life and their death. He says: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾. This is the greatest taking, the taking by death. His statement that He takes the souls, and His attribution of the action to Himself, does not contradict that He has entrusted this to the Angel of Death and his assistants, as He says: ﴿Say, "The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you"﴾ and ﴿until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail﴾. This is because He, may He be exalted, attributes things to Himself in terms of His being the Creator and the Manager, and attributes them to their causes in terms of His custom and wisdom, by which He has made a cause for every matter. His statement ﴿and the one that has not died in its sleep﴾ refers to the lesser death. That is, He holds back the soul that has not died in its sleep. ﴿So He keeps﴾ from these two souls the soul ﴿on which He has decreed death﴾, and this is the soul of one who has died, or who has been decreed to die, in his sleep, ﴿and releases﴾ the other soul ﴿until a specified term﴾; that is, until it completes its provision and its term. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾, concerning His perfect power and His giving life to the dead after their death.

This verse is evidence that the spirit (rūḥ) and the soul (nafs) are a self-subsisting body, whose substance differs from the substance of the body, and that they are created and managed, and that Allah exercises control over them in taking, holding back, and releasing. It is also evidence that the spirits of the living and of the dead meet in the barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection), where they gather and converse with one another. Allah releases the spirits of the living and holds back the spirits of the dead.

{45–46} The Exalted describes the state of the polytheists and what their polytheism entails: that when God Most High is mentioned in His unity, and commanded to be worshipped with sincere devotion, and the abandonment of what is worshipped besides Him, they recoil, flee, and detest that with the utmost aversion. {And when those besides Him are mentioned}: the idols and rivals, and when the caller calls to their worship and praises them; {behold, they rejoice}: at that, delighted by the mention of their objects of worship, and because polytheism accords with their desires. But their appointed time is the Day of Recompense; there the truth will be taken from them, and it will be seen whether their gods, which they used to call upon besides God, will avail them anything. Therefore He said: {Say: O God, Originator of the heavens and the earth}; that is, their Creator and Governor, {Knower of the unseen}: that which is hidden from our sight and knowledge, {and the seen}: that which we witness; {You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed}.

Among the greatest of differences is the difference between the sincere monotheists, who say that what they are upon is the truth and that they alone have the best reward in the Hereafter to the exclusion of others, and the polytheists who have taken rivals and idols besides You, who have equated with You those who are worth nothing, who have belittled You to the utmost degree, who rejoice at the mention of their gods and recoil at the mention of You, and yet claim that they are upon the truth while others are upon falsehood and that they alone have the best reward. And His creation indicates His knowledge: should not He who created know?

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 39, verses 49–52:

{49} He, may He be exalted, informs about the state and nature of man: that when harm touches him, whether illness, hardship, or distress, {he calls upon Us} insistently for the relief of what has befallen him. {Then, when We bestow upon him a favor from Us}: We remove his harm and lift his hardship, yet he becomes ungrateful to his Lord and denies His kindness, and {says, "I have only been given it because of knowledge"}; that is, knowledge from God that I am deserving of it and worthy of it, because I am noble in His sight, or knowledge on my part of the ways of acquiring it. God, may He be exalted, said: {Rather, it is a trial}: God tests His servants with it, to see who among them will thank Him and who will deny Him. {But most of them do not know}: therefore they regard the trial as a gift, and pure good becomes confused for them with that which may be a cause of good or of evil.

{50} God, may He be exalted, said: {Those before them had already said it}; that is, their saying: {"I have only been given it because of knowledge"}. This saying has remained passed down among the deniers, who do not acknowledge the blessing of their Lord and do not regard any right of His; their practice has continued until they were destroyed, and {what they had earned did not avail them} when the punishment came upon them.

{51} {So the evils of what they had earned befell them}: and "evils" in this context means punishments, because they distress a person and grieve him. {And those who did wrong among these people, the evils of what they earned will befall them too}: they are no better than those, and no exemption from it has been written for them in the scriptures.

{52} Having mentioned that they were deceived by wealth and, out of their ignorance, supposed that it indicates the good condition of its possessor, God, may He be exalted, informed them that His provision does not indicate that. He {extends provision to whom He wills} among His servants, whether they are righteous or wicked. {And He restricts it}: the provision; that is, He narrows it for whom He wills, whether righteous or wicked. Thus His provision is shared among creation, while faith and righteous deeds are specially bestowed upon the best of creation. {Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe}: that is, in the extending and restricting of provision, because they know that its outcome returns to wisdom and mercy, and that He is most knowing of the condition of His servants. He may restrict provision for them out of kindness to them, for if He extended it, they would transgress upon the earth. Thus He, may He be exalted, is attentive in this to the soundness of their religion, which is the basis of their happiness and success. And God knows best.

He, the Exalted, informs about His greatness and perfection, which necessitate the loss of those who disbelieve in Him. So He said: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾. This statement and others like it, which are abundant in the Qur'an, indicate that all things other than Allah are created. It therefore refutes everyone who claims that some created things are eternal, such as the philosophers (falasifa) who claim that the earth and the heavens are eternal, and those who claim that souls are eternal, and similar sayings of the people of falsehood, which imply denying that the Creator creates. The speech of Allah is not among the created things, because speech is an attribute of the speaker, and Allah, with His names and attributes, is the First, with nothing before Him. The Mu'tazila (Ahl al-I'tizal), who take from this verse and others like it that the Speech of Allah is created, are among the greatest of the ignorant, for He, the Exalted, has always been with His names and attributes. No attribute of His has come into being, and He was never without them at any time.

The proof of this is that Allah informed about His Noble Self that He is the Creator of the entire upper and lower worlds, and that He ﴿is Guardian over all things﴾. Complete guardianship necessarily requires the guardian's knowledge of what he is guardian over and his comprehensive awareness of its details, complete power over it so that he can dispose of it, preservation of what he guards, and wisdom and knowledge of the ways of management, so that he may direct and arrange it in the most fitting manner. Guardianship is not complete without all of this, and whatever is lacking from it is a deficiency in it. It is known and established that Allah is exempt from every deficiency in any of His attributes. So His informing that He is Guardian over all things indicates the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things, the completeness of His power to manage them, the completeness of His management, and the completeness of His wisdom by which He places things in their proper places.

﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning their keys in knowledge and management. ﴿Whatever mercy Allah opens for the people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him.
